rule: Four open clauses of the campaign's success criteria were blocked on a ruling no implementation lane may write, and that fact was scattered across a report section, three escalation ledgers and a verify-ledger note. Scattered, it reads as four lanes each explaining why it stopped. Collected, it is one list with a length: these are the decisions the campaign owed itself, and nothing below closed by anybody trying harder. Every row names the criterion it blocked, the artifact carrying the measurement, the question in one sentence, and what a lane may NOT do instead -- because the second half is what keeps 'blocked on a ruling' from becoming the place work goes to stop. The first four were answered on 2026-08-14 by dated amendments in the umbrella; the rows moved to answered[] rather than being deleted, so the question, its measurement and its answer stay joined. A fifth was opened the same day, by the pass that closed the other four: a criterion cannot be discharged by the lane that discovers it is unmet.
how_a_row_closes: The ruling is recorded in docs/plans/2026-08-08-silent-failure-campaign.md -- in the [H] table, in a decision row, or as a dated amendment, which is where Amendments A through D already live -- and the row moves to answered[] naming the amendment. A row does NOT close by a lane deciding the question is smaller than it looked, and it does not close by the criterion being re-read more weakly: umbrella criterion 11's own words are that a phase document may not write its own descope.
why_a_lane_may_not_write_these: Umbrella criterion 11: every [H] is either answered and recorded in the umbrella or its dependent slice is explicitly descoped there with its criterion restated -- a phase document may not write its own descope. The same reasoning reaches a success criterion an implementation would have to reinterpret to satisfy. Amendments A, B, C and D are the precedent: each was measured by a lane, refused by that lane, and recorded in the umbrella by its owner.

owed.blocks: runbook criterion 11's first clause -- every slice has a recorded verify-<slice> verdict
owed.measurement_artifact: docs/receipts/verify-ledger.json, coverage block, gated by tests/test_verify_ledger.py
owed.question: The clause has a machine denominator now and fails it backwards: 68 slice-group tags derived from commit subjects, one covered by a verdict recorded in this ledger, seven more citing a verdict in their own commit bodies with a sha a reader can open, and 61 citing nothing anywhere. R-35 was real and used -- the campaign answered NOT DISCHARGED verdicts by name -- but the verdicts were written into commit bodies rather than into an artifact, so most of them are unrecoverable as records. Does the clause bind the campaign's own past, in which case somebody schedules 61 fresh R-35 passes over closed ranges; or is it discharged forwards, by a ledger whose gate refuses the next slice group that ships without a verdict row or an explicit line?
owed.why_no_lane_may_answer_it: Both ways out are a lane deciding what a criterion means. Reading it forwards is a re-reading of 'every slice', which criterion 11's own words forbid a phase document from doing; reading it backwards commits somebody to sixty-one verification passes, which is a scheduling decision with a cost and an owner.
owed.what_a_lane_may_not_do_instead: Three things, and each has been available and refused. Manufacture a verdict for a slice nobody verified -- that is precisely the unverifiable claim about the past Phase 1 outlaws. Reconstruct verdicts from the commit bodies of the very lanes being checked, which is a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently. And shrink the denominator by declaring some tags 'not really slices', which is driving a counter to zero by editing what it counts.
owed.consequence_of_leaving_it_open: The clause holds forwards and is measured backwards. The gate refuses the next slice group that ships with neither a verdict row nor an explicit line, so the residue is a number that cannot grow in silence; what it does not do is fall.

answered.amendment: Amendment E — 2026-08-14, how a disposition transition is adjudicated
answered.the_ruling: A disposition transition is adjudicated BY CITATION, not by verdict, under three guards: the diff must be on a dispositions entry as the identity-keyed leaf_report classifies it; the cited ruling must be one a reader can open; and the leaf the entry describes may not move. The third guard is this amendment's own contribution -- citation can only ever excuse a change in what a payload SAYS ABOUT a number that did not change.
answered.blocks: umbrella criterion 1's emission clause, and umbrella criterion 7's Amendment B exit clause behind it
answered.question: When publishing a refused row's outcome as STRUCTURAL_ZERO turns a disposition string from one campaign spelling into another, R-15 classifies the diff as a text_change and R-19 sends every qualifying one to an oracle -- but R-18's export is exactly data/ and docs/math-foundations.md, so no investigator can be briefed on a question about this campaign's own disposition vocabulary. Is such a leaf adjudicated by citation, the way the 2026-08-14 R-15 amendment adjudicates a membership transition that is the ruled consequence of a declared change, or does the emission need a different landing shape entirely?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: The emission slice: the receipt view publishes a refused transition's outcome fields as StructuralZero carrying the walk's own refusal, landing against the committed coupled baseline plus one committed allowlist under R-17, owing no oracle receipt. Umbrella criterion 1's emission clause.

answered.amendment: Amendment G — 2026-08-14, D-25's one catch names a class
answered.the_ruling: D-25's “exactly one catch” is a rule about WHERE, never a count of the exception types that one handler names. The write-once ledger's raises are STARVED -- a record holding two answers for one question cannot answer either -- so the invariant table owes no fifth spelling. ProjectionStarvation's base is that class, the ledger's raises join it, the one boundary converts the base, and the source assertion allowlisting exactly one handler is unchanged in force.
answered.blocks: nothing yet -- it is a live operational risk rather than an unmet criterion
answered.question: Since the ledger join, OutcomeRewritten and DuplicateApplied are reachable on /api/calculate, /api/bis and /api/optimize, and the request boundary names only ProjectionStarvation. Does D-25's 'exactly one catch' name that exception specifically, or the class of programming errors a projection or a ledger raises on a request? If the class, does STARVED cover a rewritten outcome or does the invariant table owe a fifth spelling?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: The boundary slice: the class of programming errors that surface as a STARVED leaf gets a name, the ledger's write-once raises join it, and the one request-boundary handler converts the base -- so a contested number is a named 500 carrying a receipt instead of a bare one.

answered.amendment: Amendment H — 2026-08-14, a leaf's own adjudicating receipt
answered.the_ruling: Criterion 4 carves out a leaf's own adjudicating receipt on three conditions: the restatement sits inside an artifact adjudicating that exact leaf, it names the leaf by its path, and it agrees with the committed receipt or declares in the same artifact what it supersedes. A quotation at its address is the opposite of a second home; a second home is a figure a reader cannot trace.
answered.blocks: umbrella criterion 4's non-plan half, and runbook criterion 2's sole-home conjunct
answered.question: Criterion 4 says no receipt or commit body states a golden shape count of a committed baseline. The fingerprint counters are themselves leaves of the snapshot, so R-19 forces an oracle receipt adjudicating one to state it, R-17 forces an allowlist claiming one to state both sides, and R-34 forces a baseline-move commit to give a line of cause per moved value. Does criterion 4 carve out a leaf's own adjudicating receipt, or does the snapshot shape change so the counters are not compared leaves at all?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: Nothing to implement -- the residue was already measured and gated. What closes is the criterion: the eleven sites are the carve-out rather than eleven violations, and sole_home_scan.py --check keeps a twelfth from arriving.

answered.amendment: Amendment I — 2026-08-14, this criterion's frontend change budget
answered.the_ruling: The clause is amended to what shipped and gains the property the integer was reaching for: every commit in the campaign range touching static/js/app.js is named in the umbrella with its reason, and a commit that is not named is a budget overrun. bf4a6d3, 44331c7 and f25dcfa are named.
answered.question: Criterion 1 says static/js/app.js takes exactly one budgeted change at S9. Three commits in the campaign range touch it -- bf4a6d3 (+26), 44331c7 (+52/-10, the withheld marker the clause names) and f25dcfa (+13/-5, a row-classification refactor). Is the budget clause amended to what shipped, or are the two unbudgeted commits reverted?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: Nothing to implement, and deliberately so: reverting shipped rendering behaviour to satisfy a budget sentence is the ordering this campaign exists to invert. What closes is the clause, which now names commits instead of counting them.

why_the_answered_rows_stay: A closed row keeps its question, its measurement artifact and what the ruling unblocked. Deleting it would leave the amendment standing in the umbrella with no record of what it was answering, which is the shape -- a conclusion whose question nobody can recover -- this campaign spent four hundred commits removing.
